seo.title: Australia Summer Program | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Australia in 4 weeks: sandboarding on Stradbroke Island, a K’gari 4WD tour, kayaking in Byron Bay, surf lessons, canyoning in the Blue Mountains and conservation work. Ages 17–22.

hero.headline: Brisbane to Sydney in four weeks
hero.intro: Sandboard on Stradbroke Island, tour K’gari by 4WD, learn to surf at Crescent Head and canyon in the Blue Mountains before finishing in Sydney.

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Brisbane, Stradbroke & the road north
weeks.location: Brisbane → Stradbroke Island → Rainbow Beach, Australia
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors in Brisbane, where we spend our first days on orientation, getting to know each other and adjusting to life down under.

Then we take the ferry to Stradbroke Island for an afternoon of sandboarding and a day to explore the island. At the end of the week we head north to Rainbow Beach, with a zoo visit on the way, ready to cross to K’gari.
weeks.imageAlt: Group jumping on a beach at sunset

weeks.title: K’gari, Byron Bay & service learning
weeks.location: K’gari → Byron Bay → Crescent Head, Australia
weeks.body:
We spend three days on a 4WD tour of K’gari with Drop Bear, exploring the island with local guides. Then we drive south to Byron Bay for a day to relax and explore, and a day kayaking with dolphins.

Next we continue to Crescent Head and settle into Waves Campground, where we spend two days on a service learning project, getting our hands dirty helping to look after the local environment.
weeks.imageAlt: Group standing beside a 4WD vehicle on a wide sandy beach

weeks.title: Surf lessons & canyoning
weeks.body:
Two days of surf lessons at Crescent Head get everyone up on a board, whether it’s your first time or not. Then we travel south to the Blue Mountains and our base in Katoomba.

Here we hike to Inspiration Point and spend a day canyoning and abseiling. At the end of the week we move to The Crossing and begin our second service project with a permaculture design experience day.
weeks.imageAlt: Group in wetsuits and helmets beside a small waterfall in a canyon

weeks.title: Conservation days & Sydney
weeks.body:
Our time at The Crossing continues with a Landcare day, a bushfire prevention and wildlife tour at Potoroo Palace, and a forest regeneration day followed by an overnight hike.

Then we travel to Sydney for a day exploring the city before our program wrap, where we reflect on everything we’ve experienced together. Students fly home from Sydney the next day.
weeks.imageAlt: Group looking across the harbour to the Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge

day.heading: What a typical day looks like

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: Each week there is some designated free time to catch up on email and laundry, rest and explore with others in the group.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: Medium activity level. Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect hiking, canyoning, surfing and kayaking, and some physical work on the service projects.

items.title: Hands-on land care at The Crossing
items.body: A permaculture design experience day, a Landcare day, a forest regeneration day and a bushfire prevention and wildlife tour at Potoroo Palace.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: Do I need to know how to surf?
items.a: No. Surf lessons at Crescent Head are for all levels, so it doesn’t matter whether it’s your first time on a board.

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: The program suits anyone of average fitness with an enthusiasm for the outdoors. You don’t need experience with any of the activities, but be ready to try hiking, canyoning, surfing and kayaking. The service projects also involve some physical work.
Mostly clean, comfortable hostels and lodges, plus campground stays at Byron Bay and Crescent Head, and an overnight hike during our time at The Crossing.
Only a little. The camping level on this program is low, and you’ll spend most of your time in comfortable hostels and lodges.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
